To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
age-related changes in hepatic lipogenic activities are not due to insulin resistance but are due to decreased responsiveness to thyroid hormone.

1) the age-related decrease in lipogenic enzyme activities was not observed in the liver of rats fed a high carbohydrate diet, 2) the age-related reduction in lipogenic enzyme responsiveness to T3 was not normalized by feeding a high carbohydrate diet and 3) T3 responsiveness of lipogenic enzyme activity was reduced in the liver of aged rats.
the age-related decrease in lipogenic enzyme activity is due to resistance to the action of thyroid hormone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the age-related changes of the enzymes involved in lipogenesis.
the effects of aging on the regulation of hepatic lipogenesis.
the age-related changes of lipogenic enzyme activity and the effect of dietary manipulation on this age-related decrease in lipogenic enzyme activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decreased activity of the lipogenes enzymes in aged rats was due to a decrease in thyroid hormone responsiveness and was independent of the dietary factors tested.
the age-related changes observed in hepatic lipogenic activity are the result of a combination of factors.

the reduced lipogenic activity in aged animals is not a consequence of a reduced capacity to respond to insulin and/or thyroid hormones, but rather the consequence of an intrinsic defect in enzyme expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the age-related changes of lipogenic enzymes in liver and adipose tissue of Fischer 344 rats are not due to a primary change in enzyme activity expression, but to a change in thyroid hormone responsiveness.
the age-related changes are not due to insulin resistance, but may be due to thyroid hormone resistance.
the age-related decline in the activities of the hepatic lipogenic pathways is due to the age-related decrease in the sensitivity to thyroid hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the age-related decrease in lipogenic enzyme activity is due to a resistance to the stimulatory effect of thyroid hormone rather than an inherent decrease in the ability of the enzymes to respond to insulin.
the age-related decline in lipogenic enzymes is due to a resistance to thyroid hormone rather than an inherent change in enzyme activity expression.
the age-related changes of the lipogenic enzyme activities in rats are not due to insulin resistance but are related to thyroid hormone resistance.
